haiku-low.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine reads the same usage events and writes invoices to the shadow store only, never charging or writing the ledger.
haiku-low.q2: The new engine charges and writes the ledger. The old engine computes every invoice into the shadow store only, so it stays current, and it does not charge.
haiku-low.q3: 7 consecutive days with mismatch rate under 0.1% and at least 5,000 invoices compared. A person makes the move; nothing advances automatically.
haiku-low.q4: The automatic trigger: the new engine's charge failure rate above 2% over any 10-minute window. It can start only in both or new_only modes.
haiku-low.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only. The gates reset, so the rollout must go through shadow again and the 7-day count restarts from zero.
haiku-low.q6: Rollback from new_only stops being possible at day 35. The old engine may then be decommissioned, and the log no longer holds the events it would need.
haiku-low.q7: NOT STATED. The document only says billing_mode in the config service is the sole source of truth for the active mode.
haiku-low.q8: Gate evidence is kept in comparison_results, written by the nightly job. The document says a gate must hold before a person promotes, but names no enforcement mechanism.
haiku-low.q9: The billing monitor detects it by watching the new engine's charge failure rate. When it exceeds 2% over any 10-minute window, the monitor starts the rollback automatically.
haiku-low.q10: Charges that fall due are delayed, not dropped. Charging stays paused until resume_charging, when the old engine charges everything due and not already charged.
haiku-low.q11: Reconcile and charging both check the ledger for whether a customer's billing period is already charged, so no period is charged twice.
haiku-low.q12: Billing stays at the failed step with charging paused and on-call paged. The durable rollback record holds step status, so the rollback resumes from where it stopped; steps are safely retryable.

sonnet.q1: The old engine computes, writes the ledger and charges. The new engine's invoices go only to the shadow store (never charged, never in the ledger).
sonnet.q2: The new engine computes, writes the ledger and charges. The old engine still computes every invoice, but into the shadow store only, to stay current. It does not charge.
sonnet.q3: Gate 1 must be met: 7 consecutive days with a mismatch rate under 0.1%, and at least 5,000 invoices compared. A person makes the move (promotion is never automatic).
sonnet.q4: The automatic trigger: the new engine's charge failure rate is above 2% over any 10-minute window. It applies in both and new_only (before day 35 for new_only).
sonnet.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only. Gates reset, so the rollout must go through shadow again, with its 7-day count starting over, and then pass the gates and promotions (by a person) again.
sonnet.q6: It stops being possible at day 35 in new_only, once the old engine may be decommissioned. After that the old engine is gone and the usage event log (35-day retention) no longer holds the events it would need.
sonnet.q8: In comparison_results, written by the nightly job; the rollout tool reads it to decide whether a gate is met. What stops early promotion: gates are conditions that must hold before a person may promote, and if a gate is not met the rollout stays in its current mode. The document does not describe a technical enforcement mechanism beyond that.
sonnet.q9: The billing monitor. It watches the new engine's charge failure rate (above 2% over any 10-minute window, in both or new_only) and starts the rollback automatically.
sonnet.q10: Charging is paused during rollback, so charges that come due are delayed, not dropped. They are made at resume_charging, when the old engine charges everything that is due and not already charged.
sonnet.q11: The reconcile step compares the ledger with what the old engine says is due for each customer and billing period, and resume_charging only charges what is due and not already charged in the ledger. Charging is also paused first so nothing is charged twice during the mode change.
sonnet.q12: The rollback stays at the failing step, charging stays paused, and on-call is paged. Steps are safely retryable (each checks whether its work is already done), and the durable rollback record holds the current step and each step's status, so the rollback resumes from where it stopped. No step is skipped except catch_up when there is nothing to catch up.
